5	---
6	
7	# Card checkout
8	
9	## Summary
10	
11	Card checkout lets a shopper pay for an order by card. Merchants lose sales when paying is slow or unclear, so this feature gives shoppers one simple way to pay. Every card payment goes through an external payments gateway, and the service never stores card data. The feature is not built yet.
12	
13	## Goals served
14	
15	- G1 — Checkout that converts: card checkout is the step where a shopper turns a session into a paid order, so it directly drives the checkout conversion metric (at least 3.5% of shopper sessions by 2027-06-30).
16	
17	## Requirements
18	
19	- **R1** — A shopper can pay for an order by card.
20	- **R2** — Every card payment is processed only through an external payments gateway; the service never handles a card payment any other way.
21	- **R3** — The service does not store card data, at any point before, during or after a payment.
22	- **R4** — The shopper is told clearly whether the payment succeeded or failed.
23	- **R5** — The checkout API responds with a 95th percentile response time under 300 ms, the product-wide latency target in the hub.
24	
25	## Acceptance criteria
26	
27	- Given a shopper with an order, when they submit valid card details, then the payment is made through the external payments gateway and the shopper sees that it succeeded (R1, R2, R4).
28	- Given a payment the gateway declines or cannot complete, when the shopper submits it, then the shopper sees that the payment failed (R4).
29	- Given any card payment, when the service's code and data stores are inspected, then no card data is found and no payment route other than the gateway exists (R2, R3).
30	- Given normal load, when checkout API response times are measured, then the 95th percentile is under 300 ms (R5).
31	
32	## Dependencies
33	
34	- An external payments gateway. The choice of gateway is not yet made and is left to design.
35	
36	## Out of scope
37	
38	- Payment methods other than card.
39	- Storing card data in any form.
40	- Native mobile apps and third-party sellers, as set out in the hub.
41

1	---
2	status: "proposed"
3	version: 1
4	tickets: []
5	---
6	
7	# Order tracking
8	
9	## Summary
10	
11	Order tracking lets a shopper see where an order stands after paying for it. Shoppers are described as people who browse, pay and track orders, and they want to know where an order is. Today no order exists in the product, so this feature is not yet built. It follows card checkout: an order exists once a shopper has paid. The statuses named below are this feature's own definition, kept to the minimum needed to be testable.
12	
13	## Goals served
14	
15	- G1 — Checkout that converts. Shoppers who can see the status of what they paid for have a clearer purchase experience, which supports the checkout conversion target of at least 3.5% of shopper sessions by 2027-06-30. This feature does not have its own metric.
16	
17	## Requirements
18	
19	- **R1** — A shopper can view the current status of an order they placed.
20	- **R2** — Each order shows exactly one status at a time, taken from this list: "paid", "fulfilled".
21	- **R3** — A shopper can see only their own orders, never those of another shopper.
22	- **R4** — A merchant can mark a paid order as fulfilled, and the shopper then sees the order as "fulfilled".
23	- **R5** — Asking for an order that does not exist gives a clear "not found" answer, not an error.
24	
25	## Acceptance criteria
26	
27	- Given a shopper who has paid for an order, when they view that order, then they see the status "paid" (R1, R2).
28	- Given a paid order, when the merchant marks it as fulfilled, then the shopper sees the status "fulfilled" on their next view (R2, R4).
29	- Given two shoppers each with an order, when one asks for the other's order, then the order is not shown (R3).
30	- Given an order number that does not exist, when a shopper asks for it, then they get a "not found" answer (R5).
31	
32	## Dependencies
33	
34	- card-checkout — an order exists only once a shopper has paid through card checkout.
35	
36	## Out of scope
37	
38	- Notifications to shoppers or merchants when a status changes.
39	- Integration with shipping carriers or parcel tracking.
40	- Statuses beyond "paid" and "fulfilled", such as returns or refunds.
41	- Changes to orders by shoppers, such as cancelling.
42

2	status: "proposed"
3	version: 1
4	tickets: []
5	---
6	
7	# Saved carts
8	
9	## Summary
10	
11	A shopper who fills a cart but cannot finish paying right away should not lose it. Saved carts keeps the shopper's cart so the same shopper can come back later and carry on to card checkout. It answers the sales lost when a shopper leaves part-way and has to start again. It is not built yet.
12	
13	## Goals served
14	
15	- G1 — Checkout that converts: a kept cart lets a shopper who left before paying return and finish, which supports checkout conversion of at least 3.5% of shopper sessions by 2027-06-30.
16	
17	## Requirements
18	
19	- **R1** — When a shopper has items in a cart and leaves without paying, the cart is kept with its items and quantities.
20	- **R2** — When the same shopper returns, the kept cart is shown with the same items and quantities as when they left.
21	- **R3** — A shopper can start card checkout from a kept cart, and the cart contents carry into that checkout unchanged.
22	- **R4** — A shopper can change a kept cart (add, remove or change the quantity of an item) and the change is kept the same way.
23	- **R5** — A kept cart holds no card data.
24	- **R6** — Once a cart has been paid for through card checkout, it is no longer shown as a kept cart.
25	
26	For this feature, "the same shopper" means whatever way of recognising a returning shopper the product provides. This document does not define a sign-in or account model.
27	
28	## Acceptance criteria
29	
30	- Given a shopper with two items in a cart, when they leave without paying and return later, then the cart shows the same two items with the same quantities (R1, R2).
31	- Given a kept cart, when the shopper starts checkout, then card checkout opens with the cart's items and quantities unchanged (R3).
32	- Given a kept cart, when the shopper removes one item and returns later, then the cart shows without that item (R4).
33	- Given a kept cart, when the stored cart data is inspected, then it contains no card number, expiry date or security code (R5).
34	- Given a kept cart that the shopper has paid for through card checkout, when the shopper returns, then that cart is not offered as a kept cart (R6).
35	
36	## Dependencies
37	
38	- card-checkout — a kept cart is finished through card checkout (R3, R6).
39	
40	## Out of scope
41	
42	- How long a cart is kept before it is removed; this document sets no period.
43	- Sign-in, accounts or any other way of identifying a shopper beyond what the product already provides.
44	- Sharing a cart with another person.
45	- Reminders or messages that ask a shopper to come back to a kept cart.
46	- Storing payment details of any kind; card handling stays with card checkout and the external payments gateway.
47
